title: Peptide Vial Tray Scanning: Set Code Orientation Before Roll Approval
seoTitle: Peptide Vial Tray Scanning and Barcode Orientation
description: Plan barcode or QR placement on small research vials around the tray, scanner and application direction. Proof readability on a wrapped vial before approving the label roll.
alt: AI-generated RP Research printed vial labels in a blue tray with a handheld scanner approaching a code
caption: AI-generated tray-scanning concept with fictional RP Research labels. The printed codes are illustrative and are not verified as scannable identifiers.
intro: A code can look perfect in the PDF and still face the tray wall after a vial is loaded. Decide the scan position before releasing the roll.
sources: GS1: barcode verification and print quality

title: Mixed-Vial Research Kits: Match Each Vial Lot to the Outer Kit Record
seoTitle: Mixed-Vial Research Kit Label and Lot Matching
description: A mixed-vial research kit needs more than a shared box design. Map each inner vial identity and lot to the outer kit record before approving variable-data labels.
alt: AI-generated three distinct RP Research labelled glass vials beside a printed outer kit carton and a lot checklist
caption: AI-generated packaging concept. RP Research names and DEMO lot codes are fictional and do not document an actual filled kit or traceability system.
intro: The box may be one SKU, but the three vials inside are not one interchangeable identity. Start with the packing record.
related: Lay out batch and code fields
sources: GS1: Global Data Model attribute guide

title: Supplement Blister Cartons vs Bottles: Do Not Reuse the Same Label Artwork
seoTitle: Supplement Blister Carton vs Bottle Label Artwork
description: A blister carton and a bottle have different print surfaces and information hierarchies. Compare panel measurements, count statements, lot placement and approval ownership.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness printed supplement blister carton beside an amber 30-tablet bottle with a complete teal label
caption: AI-generated blister-and-bottle packaging comparison. The RP Wellness designs are fictional; regulatory text and package counts require brand review before commercial use.
intro: The brand can stay consistent while the artwork files change. The outer carton and a curved bottle do different jobs.
sources: FDA: Dietary Supplement Labeling Guide, Chapter I
FDA: small and multiunit package labeling guidance

title: 30 vs 60 Capsule Supplement Labels: Release Two Count Versions Without Mixing Them
seoTitle: 30 vs 60 Capsule Supplement Label Version Control
description: When a supplement moves from 30 to 60 capsules, the count and often the serving math or panel geometry change. Control proofs, roll IDs and packing line checks.
alt: AI-generated 30-capsule and 60-capsule RP Wellness amber bottles beside separately marked label proof sheets
caption: AI-generated version-control illustration. Counts and proof versions are fictional; the image does not represent approved supplement labeling.
intro: The label that says 60 should not be a quick text edit on a 30-count roll. Treat each count as a controlled artwork version.
sources: FDA: Dietary Supplement Labeling Guide, net quantity
FDA: Dietary Supplement Labeling Guide, Chapter I

title: Hologram Seals on Kraft vs Coated Cartons: Test Adhesion Before Visual Approval
seoTitle: Hologram Seal Adhesion on Kraft vs Coated Cartons
description: A hologram bridge seal may behave differently on rough kraft and coated folding board. Test the actual carton finish, seam, dwell and opening evidence before ordering.
alt: AI-generated rough kraft and coated white RP Secure cartons with holographic bridge seals over opening seams
caption: AI-generated comparison, not an RP adhesion or tamper test. A lifted corner on the kraft concept highlights a question to validate with production cartons.
intro: The same shimmering film can sit differently on a fibrous kraft box and a smooth coated carton. The finish matters as much as the artwork.
related: Place the seal across the seam
sources: HERMA: label adhesion on rough cartons
